capitals.name: Pegu Yoma jungle headquarters (near Paukkaung)
capitals.note: The page puts the leadership's headquarters 'in the Pegu Yoma near Paukkaung' (a 1963 meeting) and says the base 'was destroyed in a 1975 Tatmadaw offensive'. Paukkaung is not in the gazetteer; the coordinates are Bago town's, a stand-in. In March 1948 the leadership 'flew to their stronghold in Pyinmana'.

capitals.name: Panghsang (Pangkham)
capitals.note: The CPB page: politburo met at Panghsang in November 1978 and 'the headquarters remained there until 1989'; the page does not say when it moved there, so 1975 (the loss of the Pegu Yoma base) is a bridging reading. Pangkham was 'known before 1999 as Panghsang'; coordinates 22.167 N, 99.183 E.

notes: Rebel state added by se-04-x; the union-of-burma dossier (se-01-j) lists it among counterparts needing a dossier and draws no insurgent zones. Pages give no extent: Pegu Region and two circles (90 km at Panghsang, 60 km at Hopang, cut to Shan State) are readings. Kokang's own coordinates are on no page opened (its page gave none); the circle is placed at Hopang and covers only part of the 1,895 km2 Kokang. The Mong La NDAA (Sai Leun's splinter, 1989) and the MNDAA need dossiers; the Red Flag CPB (Thakin Soe, Arakan) is not drawn. Dates differ across pages: the mutineers stormed the HQ on 16 April (CPB page) or the Wa split was announced 17 April (Wa page); the UWSA ceasefire 18 May (text) vs 9 May (infobox). Ledger gain/loss counterparts use union-of-burma; the union-of-burma dossier has no matching events. Page budget: 6 pages including three coordinate/context pages.
